requirement: Describe the prospective assessor-blinded randomized two-arm parallel pilot feasibility trial in adults with chronic stroke, comparing neuropilates with generalized exercise.

evidence.text: The study aim, objectives and design define a randomized controlled assessor-blinded pilot feasibility comparison of the two exercise classes.

requirement: Implement assignment after baseline using computer-generated block random numbers prepared by an independent statistician not otherwise involved in the trial.

evidence.text: After baseline, patients are assigned using computer-generated block random numbers programmed by a statistician not otherwise involved.

requirement: Before finalization, specify the allocation ratio, block sizes and concealment mechanism, and clarify exactly how gender and baseline function enter randomization as stratification, minimization or another balancing rule.

evidence.text: The protocol says computer-generated block random numbers will consider gender and function but gives no ratio, block size, concealment or operational balancing rule.

requirement: Preserve assessor-only masking: the independent outcome assessor remains blinded to treatment assignment, without claiming that participants or exercise providers are blinded.

evidence.text: An independent assessor blinded to treatment assignment performs all assessments; the delivered exercise classes preclude a broader masking claim.

requirement: Represent both interventions as once-weekly supervised 60-minute classes for six weeks plus a group-specific home program twice more each week: progressive adapted neuropilates versus functional circuit-style generalized exercise.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the frequency, duration, contents, adaptation and home-program schedule for both groups.

requirement: Analyze the scheduled assessments at baseline before classes, immediately after the six-week class/home-program period, and three months after the intervention period.

evidence.text: Outcome measures are taken before and after the six-week program and at three months follow-up.

requirement: Before finalization, reconcile the primary-endpoint hierarchy: the protocol labels both Timed Up and Go and Motor Assessment Scale as primary, while the public registry lists only Motor Assessment Scale as primary and Timed Up and Go as secondary; name the governing primary endpoint or co-primary endpoints and the corresponding primary time point.

evidence.text: Under Primary, the protocol lists Gait analysis: Timed Up & Go and Motor Assessment Scale for stroke.

notes: The frozen ClinicalTrials.gov registry snapshot lists Motor Assessment Scale as primary and Timed Up and Go as secondary. The registry is provenance evidence, not a model-visible substitute for the protocol.

requirement: Before finalization, define the Motor Assessment Scale endpoint as a prespecified total or component score, its direction of benefit, the baseline and post-baseline values used, and the primary change or follow-up contrast.

evidence.text: The protocol names Motor Assessment Scale as primary but does not define total versus component scoring or the primary contrast.

requirement: Before finalization, define the Timed Up and Go endpoint, including the unit in seconds, replicate handling if applicable, direction of benefit, and the baseline-to-follow-up quantity used in analysis.

evidence.text: The protocol names Timed Up and Go gait analysis but gives no statistical derivation.

requirement: Treat Oxford muscle-strength grade, Modified Ashworth spasticity, Functional Independence Measure and London Handicap Scale as distinct secondary outcomes rather than combining them into an unspecified composite.

evidence.text: The protocol lists strength, spasticity and two functional scales as separate secondary outcomes.

requirement: Before finalization, operationalize feasibility outcomes for class delivery and participation, including denominators and summaries for attendance, prescribed home-exercise completion or training diaries, exercise modification, and supportive-equipment need.

evidence.text: Feasibility and supportive-equipment need are objectives; the intervention permits adaptations and asks participants to keep home-training diaries.

requirement: Before finalization, define adverse-effect collection and analysis, including the safety population, exercise-exposure window, event categories, severity and relatedness, withdrawals due to events, and arm-level incidence summaries.

evidence.text: Investigating adverse effects of group neuropilates is a stated objective, but collection and analysis rules are absent.

requirement: For the reference plan's descriptive within-arm assessment, use paired t tests to compare baseline with the immediate post-six-week value separately within the neuropilates and generalized-exercise groups.

evidence.text: Paired T tests will be used to compare before and after data in both groups.

notes: This records the reference SAP decision only. A within-arm paired test is not a valid substitute for the randomized between-group treatment contrast.

requirement: Before finalization, select a primary randomized treatment-effect analysis that directly compares neuropilates with generalized exercise, such as baseline-adjusted follow-up analysis or a group-by-time model; do not infer efficacy from significance in one arm and nonsignificance in the other.

evidence.text: The randomized objective compares effects between the two classes at repeated assessments.
The reference mentions only within-group paired t tests and leaves the randomized contrast undefined.

requirement: Before finalization, prespecify how the immediate post-six-week and three-month repeated outcomes enter the model, including fixed effects for randomized group, visit and group-by-visit interaction, participant-level correlation, covariance structure and target visit contrasts.

evidence.text: The protocol schedules baseline, post-six-week and three-month assessments, but the reference SAP does not model the three-month visit.

requirement: Before finalization, define the primary analysis population and retain treatment attribution by randomized assignment, with explicit rules for participants who attend no classes, cross over, discontinue exercise, or lack any post-baseline assessment.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomized classes and home exercise but no analysis set or treatment-attribution rules.

requirement: Before finalization, define item-level missing-score rules, handling of missed post-six-week and three-month assessments, the primary missing-data assumption, and at least one sensitivity analysis appropriate to dropout in a small exercise trial.

evidence.text: Three assessment times and multiple scales are defined without missing-data rules.
The reference paired-test statement contains no missing-data assumption or sensitivity analysis.

requirement: Before finalization, declare whether the pilot is estimation-focused or confirmatory and, if any hypothesis is confirmatory, specify the family, two-sided alpha, multiplicity control and success rule across endpoints, visits and contrasts.
acceptable_values: multiplicity procedure or explicit exploratory interpretation

evidence.text: The pilot has multiple clinical, feasibility and safety objectives at multiple visits but no hierarchy or success criterion.

requirement: Before finalization, specify arm-by-visit summaries, the treatment-effect measure, two-sided confidence interval and direction of benefit for each analyzed outcome; report effect-size uncertainty rather than p-values alone.

evidence.text: The reference names paired t tests but no estimates, confidence intervals, summaries or directions of benefit.

requirement: Before finalization, document the prospective recruitment target, anticipated allocation by arm, feasibility or precision rationale and attrition allowance; do not substitute the later registry actual enrollment of 30 for a missing prospective calculation.

evidence.text: The protocol only says it is hoped that two neuropilates classes of seven to eight participants will run and gives no total target or calculation.

notes: Registry enrollment is execution-era information and must not be presented as a prospectively justified target.

requirement: Before using paired t tests, prespecify the paired-difference normality assessment and a robust or nonparametric fallback; select scale-appropriate methods for ordinal Oxford and Modified Ashworth outcomes rather than applying an unqualified t test to every measure.

evidence.text: The outcome set includes ordinal Oxford and Modified Ashworth scales.
The SAP applies paired t tests to before-after data without assumptions or scale-specific qualifications.

requirement: Before finalization, prespecify baseline descriptive summaries and any adjustment for gender and baseline function used in randomization, without conducting or interpreting baseline significance tests as evidence of randomization success.

evidence.text: Gender and function are said to be considered in block randomization, but analysis adjustment and baseline reporting are unspecified.
